summary: Stdcall 3DNow! bilinear interpolation between three reference points. Given a base point a2, an x-delta point a3 and a y-delta point a4 (each a packed pair of floats), with two scalar weights a5 (x) and a6 (y), it writes a1[0] = a2[0] + (a3[0]-a2[0])*w0 + (a4[0]-a2[0])*w1 as a full packed pair and a1[1] as the low-dword scalar cvtsi64_si32(a2[1].lo + (a3[1].lo-a2[1].lo)*w0 + (a4[1].lo-a2[1].lo)*w1). The weights are broadcast with punpckldq, each reference value is scaled by its weight via pfsub/pfmul and combined with pfadd. Emits _m_femms() before returning the destination pointer a1. No branches or calls.

local_names.a5: x weight w0 (scalar, treated as float via cvtsi32_si64)
local_names.a6: y weight w1 (scalar, treated as float via cvtsi32_si64)
local_names.v7: base scalar for the second component, cvtsi32_si64(a2[1].m64_u32[0])
local_names.v10: w0 broadcast to both lanes (punpckldq of v6)
local_names.v11: w1 broadcast to both lanes (punpckldq of v8)

operations.description: Load the x weight scalar v6 = cvtsi32_si64(a5).
Load the base scalar v7 = cvtsi32_si64(a2[1].m64_u32[0]) used for the second output component.
Load the y weight scalar v8 = cvtsi32_si64(a6).
Broadcast both weights: v10 = punpckldq(v6, v6) and v11 = punpckldq(v8, v8).

Compute second-component scalar v12 = pfadd(pfadd(pfmul(pfsub(cvtsi32_si64(a3[1].m64_u32[0]), v7), v10), v7), pfmul(pfsub(cvtsi32_si64(a4[1].m64_u32[0]), v7), v11)): base + (a3.1-base)*w0 + (a4.1-base)*w1.

Write first output pair a1->m64_u64 = pfadd(pfadd(pfmul(pfsub(a3[0], a2[0]), v10), a2[0]), pfmul(pfsub(a4[0], a2[0]), v11)): base + (a3-base)*w0 + (a4-base)*w1 for both lanes, into the low output slot at this+0x0.
Write second-component scalar a1[1].m64_i32[0] = cvtsi64_si32(v12) into the high output slot at this+0x8.
Execute _m_femms() before returning to clear 3DNow!/MMX state.

unresolved: The consumer of this bilinear interpolation (e.g. terrain heightfield, camera path, texture/sampling path) is not established by this packet alone.
The weights a5/a6 are declared unsigned int in the prototype but are reinterpreted as floats by cvtsi32_si64; the bit-level float values supplied by callers are outside this packet.
Packet field base 'this' covers only the output pointer a1; the reference points a2/a3/a4 have no identity in the fact table.
